newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas up in Q1 despite wide bid/offer spread.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas up in Q1 despite wide bid/offer spread.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures strengthened in the first quarter on Monday, with both January and February trading at higher.
January traded 25 lots at 17.70 pence a therm, up by 0.12 pence from Friday's settlement level, while February was up by 0.06 pence to 17.80 pence a therm
A futures broker pointed out that it was surprising the two months had been done at such high prices when the bid was well below this for most of the morning.
"The question is if the bid and offer are so wide, how come it gets hit right at the offer?" he asked.
By the close of the session January and February were bid at 17.30 pence and 17.40 pence respectively.
Transco announced details of its storage gas tender on Monday morning.
The company said bids were received for comfortably in excess of the volume offered and it the gas was sold at an average price of 9.45 pence a therm.
But a futures broker said it was unlikely there was a connection between the Transco tender and the price rise on futures.
